Section 1.3    Transition Rules .
(a)    Supplemental Benef its. Each Participant’ s accrued benefit under the Prior SRP Plan as of December 31, 2004
(“Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits ”) was determined by the Administrator in accordance with Section 409A  of the Code and
Notice 2005-1. Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits are governed by and administered in accordance with the Prior SRP Plan,
provided, however , that any election with respect to Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits may not materially modify the rights,
terms or conditions of the Prior SRP  Plan.
(b)    Deferral Benefits . Deferral Benefits have been provided under the Deferral Plan, which for Plan Years ending on
or before December 31, 2007, was the American Express Salary Deferral Plan, the American Express Pay-for -Performance Deferral
Programs and any other similar non-qualified plans for the deferral of compen sation available in such Plan Years (collectively , the
“Prior Deferral Plan”), and for Plan Years beginning on or after January 1, 2008, is this Plan. The Deferral Benefits that were earned
and vested prior to January 1, 2005 (the “Grandfathered Defe rral Benefits ”) remained subject to the Prior Deferra l Plan. Effective
October 27, 2010, earnings credits on Grandfathered Deferral Benefits were administered in accordance with Article 7 of this Plan.
Finally , such amendments also provided  that in the event of a Change in Contr ol, additional earnings credits due as a result of the
Change in Control under the terms of the Prior Deferral Plan shall be credited at the AFR, as defined herein. All other benefits have
been governed by and administered solely in accordance with the Plan, as amended and restated from time to time. Effective
January 1, 2011, the Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits lost their Grandfathered Benefits status and were distributed in
accordance with Section 1.4 below . All other Grandfathered Deferral Benefits (including any remaining Grandfathered Deferral
Benefits attributable to Degrandfathere d Participants) shall continue to be Grandfathered Deferral Benefits, subject to the Prior
Deferral Plan.
(c)    For conveni ence of reference, the details regarding the form and timing of payment of Grandfathered
Supplemental Benef its, Grandfathered Deferral Benefits, and/or Formerly Gran dfathered Deferral Benefits may be set forth on an
Appendix to this Plan document, which may be updated or clarified by the Administrator from time to time (provided that such an
Appendix shall not alter the form or timing of payment of such benefits from the form and timing provided for by this Section, the
Prior SRP  Plan and the Prior Deferral Plan, as applicable).

title: Modification of Certain Grandfathered Benefits
heading: Section 1.4 Modification of Certain Grandfather ed Benefits .
start_phrase: Effective January 1, 2011, the Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits of each Degrandfathered Participant which are not scheduled to be in pay status by December 31, 2016 shall be payable in a lump sum on March 1, 2012 unless otherwise elected pursuant to Section 1.4(b).
summary:
- Establishes that the plan is governed by ERISA and related DOL regulations, and references compliance with Code Section 409A and IRS Notice 2005-1.
- Sets the effective date of the amended and restated plan as January 1, 2023, with clarifying provisions applied retroactively to original intent.
- Provides transition rules for legacy benefits:
  - Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits (accrued under the Prior SRP Plan as of December 31, 2004) remain under the Prior SRP Plan and cannot be materially modified.
  - Deferral Benefits were provided under prior nonqualified deferral plans through 2007; this Plan governs from 2008 forward.
  - Pre-2005 Grandfathered Deferral Benefits remain under the Prior Deferral Plan; from October 27, 2010, their earnings credits follow Article 7 of this Plan.
  - In a Change in Control, additional earnings under the Prior Deferral Plan are credited at the AFR.
  - Effective January 1, 2011, certain Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits lost grandfathered status and were distributed per Section 1.4; remaining grandfathered benefits continue under the Prior Deferral Plan.
  - An Appendix may summarize payment form/timing for grandfathered benefits for reference without altering those terms.
- Modifies certain grandfathered benefits (Section 1.4):
  - Effective January 1, 2011, Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits not in pay status by December 31, 2016 are paid in a lump sum on March 1, 2012 unless a timely alternate election was made.
  - Earnings on these amounts are credited under the Interest Credit Method through December 31, 2011; for Executive Officers, credits are capped at the AFR (with limited exceptions); earnings for early 2012 are at the AFR.
  - By December 31, 2010, participants could elect lump sum or 5/10/15 annual installments, payable on a specified date no earlier than July 1, 2017 or at Retirement (no earlier than July 1, 2017), with specific timing rules upon Separation from Service and 90-day administrative payment windows.
  - Death before completion of payments is handled under Section 8.4 for Post-2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - Such elections become effective January 1, 2012; if payment was delayed, credits remain under the Interest Credit Method through 2011, then switch to the Hypothetical Investment Method as of January 1, 2012; AFR cap for Executive Officers applies.
- Begins Article 2 (Definitions) and defines “Account” as the combination of a Participant’s Deferral Account and Supplemental Account.
text:
Section 1.4    Modification of Certain Grandfather ed Benefits .
(a)    Effective January 1, 2011, the Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits of each Degrandfathered Participant
which are not scheduled to be in pay status by December 31,
-5-2016 shall be payable in a lump sum on March 1, 2012 unless otherwise elected pursuant to Section 1.4(b). Formerly Grandfathered
Deferral Benefits which are scheduled for payment on March 1, 2012 will be credited with earnings under the Interest Credit Method
through December 31, 2011, provided, however , that if a Participant becomes an Executive Officer, earnings credited to such
Participant’ s Former ly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits shall not exceed the AFR (except to the extent earnings in excess of the AFR
have been paid out prior to the Participa nt’s becoming an Executive Officer). For the portion of 2012 prior to the date of payment,
earnings on Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits shall be credited with earnings at the AFR.
(b)    On or before  December 31, 2010, each Degrandfathered Participant could elect to have his or her formerly
Grandfathered Deferral Benefits paid to him or her in a lump sum or five, 10 or 15 substantially equal annual installments, and (i) on
a specified date (which must be a January 1 or July 1) that is no earlier than July 1, 2017 (or as soon thereafter as administratively
practicable, but no later than 90 days), or (ii) upon his or her Retirement (but no earlier than July 1, 2017), and in the case of a
Participant who elected installment payments, payment will continue as of each subsequent January 1 or July 1, whichever is
applicable (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days); provided that a Degrandfathered
Participant who elects to be paid at Retirement or who elects a specified date and experiences a Separation from Service prior to the
selected specified date shall have Defer ral Benefits paid as of the later of (i) July 1, 2017 or (ii) the January 1 or July 1 which is at
least six months following his or her Separation from Service (or, in either case, as soon thereafter as administratively practicable,
but no later than 90 days), provided that in the case of an election of installment payments, payment will commence as of the later of
July 1, 2017 or the July 1 in the calendar year following the year of Separation from Service and continue each July 1 thereafter (or
as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days). If a Participant dies before payment is completed,
payment shall be handled in accordance with Section 8.4 as applicable to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits. In any event, such subsequent
election shall not become effective until January 1, 2012. If a Degrandfathered Participant files an election to delay payment, his or
her Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits will be credited with earnings under the Interest Credit Method through December 31,
2011, provided, however , that if a Participant becomes an Executive Officer, earnings credited to such Participant’ s Formerly
Grandfathered Deferral Benefits shall not exceed the AFR (except to the exten t earnings in excess of the AFR have been paid out
prior to the Participant’ s becoming an Executive Officer). Such Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits shall transition to the
Hypothetical Investment Method as of January 1, 2012.

title: Definitions
heading: Section 2.1 Definitions .
start_phrase: As used in the Plan, the following terms have the meanings indicated below:
summary:
- Payment and earnings rules for Formerly Grandfathered/Degrandfathered Deferral Benefits:
  - Amounts scheduled for March 1, 2012 payout receive Interest Credit Method earnings through December 31, 2011; any period in 2012 before payment earns at AFR.
  - If a participant becomes an Executive Officer, credited earnings on Formerly Grandfathered amounts are capped at AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR before that status change).
  - By December 31, 2010, Degrandfathered Participants could elect lump sum or 5/10/15 annual installments, payable on a specified Jan 1 or Jul 1 no earlier than July 1, 2017, or upon Retirement (not earlier than July 1, 2017).
  - If Separation from Service occurs before the selected date, payment begins the later of July 1, 2017 or at least six months after separation; installment payments start the later of July 1, 2017 or July 1 of the year after separation and continue each July 1.
  - Death before completion is handled per Section 8.4 (Post-2010 Deferral Benefits rules).
  - Any subsequent election becomes effective January 1, 2012.
  - If payment is delayed by election, earnings continue under the Interest Credit Method through December 31, 2011 (subject to AFR cap for Executive Officers), then switch to the Hypothetical Investment Method as of January 1, 2012.

- Article 2: Key plan definitions and governance:
  - Core plan entities and roles: Administrator (Employee Benefits Administration Committee), Committee (Compensation and Benefits Committee), Investment Committee, Company (Amex and certain affiliates).
  - Accounts and benefits: Deferral Account, Supplemental Account (RP-Related and RSP-Related), Deferral Benefits, Supplemental Benefits, Supplemental Distributions, and related elections.
  - Participant categories and status: Participant, Employee, Executive Officer (Band 99), Non-Executive Officer, Degrandfathered Participant, Retiree, Retirement, Retirement Eligible, Former GE Employees.
  - Compensation and pay bases: Base Salary, Incentive Pay, and references to Total Pay; exclusions to prevent duplication with non-qualified deferrals.
  - Timing constructs: Plan Year (separate definitions for Supplemental vs. Deferral Benefits), Band 50 Determination Date, Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date.
  - Pre-/Post-2010 distinctions: Post-2010 and Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits; Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits becoming subject to this Plan as of January 1, 2011.
  - Credit/economic measures: AFR (120% applicable federal long-term rate), Schedule Rate, Minimum Schedule Rate, Moody’s A Rate, Stock Fund.
  - Legal and compliance references: Code, Section 409A (and policy), Section 401(a)(17) compensation limits, Section 415 limitations, Exchange Act Section 16(a) (Insiders), Employment Arbitration Policy, Severance Plan references, Trust (grantor trust).
  - Events and conditions: Separation from Service, Disability (per 409A), Unforeseeable Emergency, Beneficiary.
  - Cross-references and interpretation: Undefined terms follow Qualified Retirement Plan meanings; grammatical rules for gender/number.

title: Administrator
heading: Section 3.1 Administrator .
start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Administrator .
summary:
- Article 3 (Administration):
  - The Plan is administered by an Administrator.
  - The Administrator has broad authority to interpret, construe, and administer the Plan; correct defects, omissions, inconsistencies, and mathematical/accounting errors through equitable adjustments.
  - Decisions are final, conclusive, and binding on all Participants and Beneficiaries.
  - The Administrator may delegate authority and responsibilities; references to the Administrator include delegates to the extent of delegation.
  - The Administrator’s authority operates except as otherwise provided by the Committee and subject to limitations in Section 10.7.

- Article 4 (Eligibility):
  - Participation is limited to Employees meeting Section 4.2 and occurs automatically for those Employees.
  - The Administrator may exclude specific Employees or categories from all or parts of the Plan.
  - Eligibility must be consistent with the Plan’s status as a “top-hat” plan under ERISA.
  - Unless determined otherwise, Employees must be in Band 35 or above to be eligible.

- Section 4.2 (Participation requirements):
  - Employee must satisfy Section 4.1 and be a participant in a Company-maintained Qualified Retirement Plan (per that plan’s eligibility rules).
  - For the relevant Plan Year, the Employee must either:
    - Have an Account from a prior Plan Year (including being treated as having one if the Employee declined a prior participation offer), or
    - Receive Total Pay (as defined under the RSP, disregarding the Section 401(a)(17) limitation) exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) limit.

summary:

      - Accrue benefits under a Qualified Retirement Plan in excess of the Section 415 limit.

title: Benefits Under the RP
heading: Section 5.1 Benefits Under the RP.
start_phrase: If a Parti cipant is a participant under the RP, other than a terminated participa nt, the Company shall establish an RP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as follows:
summary:
- Eligibility highlights: participants include those in pay Band 50 or higher as of the Band 50 Determination Date (with Administrator discretion to include newly hired/promoted Band 50 employees for open enrollment) or those whose Qualified Retirement Plan benefits exceed the IRC Section 415 limit.
- Article 5 establishes supplemental benefits that provide make-up credits above qualified plan limits.

- Section 5.1 (RP supplemental benefits):
  - An RP-Related Account is created for eligible, non-terminated participants.
  - Compensation for RP credits follows the RP definition, with Committee discretion to modify; beginning with the 2003 performance year, includes certain restricted stock granted in lieu of cash supplemental Annual Incentive Awards.
  - Contribution Credits equal the excess of hypothetical RP credits calculated without the IRC Section 401(a)(17) compensation cap and including deferrals, over actual RP credits; no credits for pay periods on/after July 1, 2007.
  - Benefit formula is set by the Administrator and applied uniformly to similarly situated participants.
  - Additional Years of Service:
    - Company may, by special agreement, deem five additional Years of Service and credit the difference between cumulative credits with and without the added service; default five-year vesting with forfeiture upon termination before five years, except for death or disability.
    - Transition: participants with such agreements who lack five Years of Service as of July 1, 2007 receive 2007 credits as if the RP continued through December 31, 2007; no credits for 2008 or later.

- Section 5.2 (RSP supplemental benefits):
  - An RSP-Related Account is created for eligible, non-terminated participants.
  - Compensation for RSP credits equals “Total Pay” under the RSP, subject to Committee discretion; effective July 1, 2007, includes restricted stock granted in lieu of cash Annual Incentive Awards (subject to a cap).
  - Limitation for Band 50+ participants: Incentive Pay (including such restricted stock) counted only up to one times Base Salary; pay band/Base Salary determined as of January 1 (or upon hire/rehire); special rehire rule for contributions; limitation applies to amounts actually paid in the Plan Year, regardless of when earned.

Section 5.1    Benefits Under  the RP. If a Parti cipant is a participant under the RP, other than a terminated participa nt, the
Company shall establish an RP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as follows:

granted to certain Participants in lieu of cash supplemental Annual Incentive Awards.
(b)    Contribution Credit s. There shall be credited to a Participa nt’s RP-Related Account for each Plan Year, in

title: Benefits in Excess of Limits Under the RSP
heading: Section 5.2 Benefits in Excess of Limits Under the RSP .
start_phrase: If a Participant is a participant in the RSP, other than a terminated participant, the Company shall establish an RSP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as follows:
summary:
- Establishes special RP-related credits for certain participants with individual agreements to make up benefits, calculated under Section 5.3, generally subject to five-year vesting and forfeiture upon termination other than death or disability. Participants with fewer than five Years of Service as of July 1, 2007 receive a 2007 Plan Year credit as if the RP remained in effect through December 31, 2007; no credits are provided for 2008 or later.
- Creates an RSP-Related Account for active RSP participants to provide benefits that exceed qualified plan limits:
  - Defines Compensation for RSP credits by reference to “Total Pay” under the RSP, with Committee discretion to modify; effective July 1, 2007 includes restricted stock granted in lieu of cash annual incentives, subject to limits.
  - Imposes a Band 50+ limitation excluding Incentive Pay (including in-lieu restricted stock) above one times Base Salary; pay band/Base Salary determined as of January 1 (or rehire date); Incentive Pay counted when paid. Temporary salary reductions from March 30, 2009 through January 3, 2010 are disregarded.
  - Contribution Credits:
    - Company Stock Contribution: 1% make-up on Compensation plus deferrals over qualified limits, reduced by actual RSP allocation; no credits for pay periods on/after July 1, 2007.
    - Company Profit-Sharing Contribution: make-up of discretionary/fixed-rate profit-sharing over Section 401(a)(17)/415 limits and deferrals; only vested portions are payable, non-vested forfeited.
    - Company Matching Contribution (effective January 1, 2017):
      - Match on nonqualified deferrals up to 6% of Compensation not counted under the RSP due to Section 401(a)(17) limits or deferrals (regardless of RSP contributions).
      - Additional match equal to what was excluded under the RSP solely due to Section 415 limits.
      - Vesting follows the RSP.
    - Company Conversion Contribution: make-up of conversion contributions over limits; none after December 31, 2017 for Band 50+ and after December 31, 2018 for below Band 50; suspended March 30, 2009–January 3, 2010 except for those retirement-eligible as of December 31, 2009; resumed thereafter at prior levels; only vested portions payable; Company reserves right to change.
    - Transition Contributions for certain Former GE Capital employees: make-up of RSP transition contributions until they expire (no contributions after March 31, 2011); if eligible for both conversion and transition, participant receives the greater; only vested portions payable.
    - No disability-related contributions are provided under this plan.
  - Additional Company Contribution for Additional Years of Service: for selected participants deemed to have five extra RSP Years of Service, an additional credit equal to 80% (or a lower agreed percentage) of base salary at hire, generally five-year vested with forfeiture on termination other than death/disability; calculated and credited per Section 5.3 and any special agreement.
- Section 5.3 governs crediting: timing and manner determined by the Administrator, generally mirroring qualified plans but not required; amounts related to RP Section 415 limitations may be estimated at Separation from Service using consistent, reasonable assumptions.
text:
Section 5.2    Benefits in Excess of Limits Under  the RSP . If a Participant is a participant in the RSP, other than a
terminated participant, the Company shall establish an RSP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as
follows:
(a)    “Compensation” for RSP  Credits .
(i)    Definition . For purposes of RSP credits under this Section 5.2, “Compensation ” has the meaning given
the term “Total Pay” in the RSP, provided that the Committee may, in its discretion, designate additional or different items as
Compensation for purposes of this Section 5.2. Effective July 1, 2007, “Compensation” for purposes of RSP credits under this
Section 5.2 shall include the value of restricted stock awards granted to certain Participants in lieu of cash Annual Incentive Awards,
subject to the limitation set forth in Section 5.2(a)(ii).
(ii)    Limitation . “Compensation” of a Participant who is in Band 50 or above for purposes of RSP credits
under this Section 5.2 shall not include any Incentive Pay (including the value of any restricted stock awards granted to certain
Participants in lieu of cash Annual Incentive Awards) in excess of one times his or her Base Salary . For purposes of this provision, a
Participant’ s pay band and Base Salary shall be determined as of January 1 of each Plan Year (or, if the Participant was not employed
as an Eligible Empl oyee on January 1, the date the Participant becomes or is rehired as an Eligible Employee, and in the case of a
Participant who terminates employment and is rehired as an Eligible Employee within the same Plan Year, the application of this rule
shall be determined by pay band as of the date of rehire as an Eligible Employee with respect to Company contributions other than
those accrued (and as to which the Participant had met all the prerequisites for receipt) prior to rehire). In addition, Incentive Pay
subject to this limitation shall only be those amounts actually paid in the Plan Year, regardless of when such amounts were earned.
-14-(iii)    Temporary Salary Reductions Disregarded. In determining the Compensation of a Participant for
purposes of this Section 5.2, “Total Pay” under the RSP shall be determined by disregarding the temporary salary reductions in effect
for the pay period commencing March 30, 2009 through the pay period ending on January 3, 2010.
(b)    Contribution Credits . The following amounts shall be credited to the Participant’ s RSP-Related Acco unt for each
Plan Year, in accordance with Section 5.3:
(i)    Company Stock Contribution . An amou nt equal to: (A) one percent of the sum of: (1) the Participant’ s
Compensation, calculated without the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation or Section 415 Limitations, plus (2) that portion of a
Participant’ s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan, minus (B) the amount actually allocated as a
Company Stock Contribution to the account of the Participant under the RSP. For purposes of this Section 5.2(b)(i), the
Section 401(a)(17) Limitation shall be deemed to apply pro ratably to each regularly scheduled pay period for each Plan Year. No
credits shall be made to a Participant’ s RSP-Related Account pursuant to this Section 5.2(b)(i) for any pay period ending on or after
July 1, 2007.
(ii)    Company Profit-Sharing Contribution . An amount equal to: (A) the Company Profit-Sharing
Contribution percen tage utilized for purposes of the RSP for that Plan Year for such Participant (which, for the avoidance of doubt,
shall be the percentage utilized for any Company Discretionary Profit Sharing Contribution and/or Company Fixed Rate
Contribution, as applicable) times the sum of: (1) the Participant’ s Compensation, calculated without the Section 401(a)(17)
Limitation or Section 415 Limitations, plus (2) that portion of a Participant’ s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant
to a Defer ral Plan, minus (B) the amount actually allocated as a Company Profit-Sharing Contribution (which, for the avoidance of
doubt, shall be the amount actually allocated as a Company Discretionary Profit Sharing Contribution and/or Company Fixed Rate
Contribution, as applicable) to the Account of the Participant under the RSP. Unless otherwise expressly provided in the Plan,
benefits credited under this Section 5.2(b)(ii) at the time of a Supplemental Distribution shall be restricted to a Participant’ s vested
portion, as determined under the applicable provisions of the RSP. Any non-ves ted portion of such deferred compensation to be paid
shall be forfeited.
(iii)    Company Matching Contribution .
(A)    Effective with Compensation paid on or after January 1, 2017, each eligible Participant who
meets the eligibility requirements for a Qualified Matching Contribution (or other type of matching contribution) under the RSP (but
without regard to whether or not he or she contributes under the RSP) shall receive a Matching Contribution each Plan Year equal to
the Participant’ s salary reduction amou nt (from Base Salary , Incentive Pay or a combination of both) contributed pursuant to a
Deferral Election under Article 6 for such Plan Year (up to a maximum of six percent of the Participant’ s Compensation which is not
counted under the RSP either because it is in excess of the Section 401(a)(17)  Limitation for the Plan Year or because it has been
deferred under a Deferral Plan). Compe nsation for this purpose will not include amounts paid prior to a Participant’ s Entry Date
under the RSP  with respect to Qualified Matching Contributions (or other type of matching contributions, as applicable).
-15-(B)    Separately from any Matching Contribution calculated under (A), a Participant will be provided
a Matching Contribution equal to the amount of Qualified Matching Contribution (or other type of matching contribution) that
would have been provided to the Participant under the RSP, but was not able to be provided solely on account of the limitations of
Section 415 of the Code.
(C)    The vesting of Matching Contributions will parallel the vesting rules applicable under the RSP .
(iv)    Company Conversion Contribution .
(A)    Except as otherwise provided by Section 5.2(b)(iv)(B), an amount equal to: (1) the Company
Conversion Contribution percentage utilized for purposes of the RSP for that Plan Year for such Participant times the sum of: (a) the
Participant’ s Compensation, calculated without the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation or Section 415 Limitations, plus (b) that portion of
a Participa nt’s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan, minus (2) the amount actually allocated as
a Compan y Conversion Contribution to the Account of the Participant under the RSP. Unless otherwise expressly provided in the
Plan, bene fits credited under this Section 5.2(b)(iv)(A) at the time of a Supplemental Distribution shall be restricted to a Participant’ s
vested portion, as determined under the applicable provisions of the RSP. Any non-vested portion of such deferred compensation to
be paid shall be forfeited. Pursuant to the terms of the RSP, no Company Conversion Contributions are made for periods after
December 31, 2017 for employees in Band 50 and above, or for periods after December 31, 2018 for employees below Band 50;
accordingly , no Company Conversion Contributions are made under the Plan for such periods.
(B)    No Company conversion contributions were made for the pay period commencing March 30,
2009 through the pay period ending January 3, 2010 to any Participant; provided, however , the preceding limitation did not apply to
Participants who were Retirement Eligible as of December 31, 2009. For the avoidance of doubt, when Company conversion
contributions resumed after the pay period ending on January 3, 2010, such contributions resumed in the same amount as in effect
immediately prior to the pay period beginning on March 30, 2009; provided, however, that the Company continued to retain the right
to modify , amend or terminate the Plan and any contributions thereunder at any time for any reason whatsoever .
(v)    Transition Contributions for Certain Former GE Capital Employees . For Former GE Employees, an
amount equal to: (A) the Transition Contribution percentage utilized for purpos es of the RSP for that Plan Year for such Participant
times the sum of: (1) the Participant’ s Compensation, calculated without the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation or Section 415
Limitations, plus (2) that portion of a Participant’ s Compensation deferred durin g such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan, minus
(B) the amount actually allocated as a Transition Contribution to the Account of the Participant under the RSP. Notwithstanding the
foregoing, if an individual would be eligible for both Company Conversion Contributions under Section 5.2(b)(iv) and Transition
Contributions under this Section 5.2(b)(v), such individual shall only receive the greater of the Company Conversion Contributions
and the Transition Contributions to which he or she would otherwise be entitled during such period of dual eligibility . Unless
otherwise expressly provided in the Plan, benefits credited under this
-16-Section 5.2(b)(v) at the time of a Supplemental Distribution shall be restricted to a Participant’ s vested portion, as determined under
the applicable provisions of the RSP. Any non-vested portion of such deferred compensation to be paid shall be forfeited. The right
to Transiti on Contributions under this Section shall expire at the same time as the right to Transition Contributions under the RSP.
Pursuant to the terms of the RSP , no Transition Contributions are made for periods after March 31, 201 1.
(vi)    No Disability Contributions . The RSP provides for certain contributions to be made on account of
qualifying RSP participants who are “disabled” as defined under the RSP. For the avoidance of doubt, this Plan does not provide for
such continuing contributions on account of a disability .
(c)    Company Contribution for Additional Years of Service . Certain Participant s, as determined by the Company in
its sole discretion, may be deemed to have rendered five additional Years of Service under the RSP. For each such Participant, for the
period of January 1, 2008 and thereafte r, subject to such terms and conditions as the Company may impose upon such benefits by
special agreement with such Participant (in the event of a conflict with this Section 5.2(c), such special agreement shall control), an
additional amount shall be credited to the Participant’ s RSP-Related Account equal to 80 percent (or such lower percentage specified
in the special agreement) of the Participant’ s annual rate of base salary (as of the Participant’ s date of hire), before any reduction for
any amoun ts deferred by the Participant pursuant to Section 401(k) or Section 125 of the Code, or pursuant to a Deferral Plan or any
other non-qualified plan which permits the voluntary deferral of compensation . Subject to the terms of the special agreement with
each such Participan t, such amounts shall be calculated under procedures to be determined from time to time by the Administrator
and consistently applied to similarly situated Participants. Unless otherwise determined by the Administrator or agreed in the special
agreement with the Participant, amounts credited under this Section 5.2(c) shall be subject to five-year vesting, and such amounts
shall be forfeited by the Participant if the Participant’ s service with the Com pany terminates for any reason other than death or
disability (as defined in the RSP) before five years of actual service have been rendered to the Company by such Participant.
Amounts described in this Section 5.2(c ) shall be credited to the RSP-Related Account established for the Participant in accordance
with Section 5.3.

title: Crediting of Account
heading: Section 5.3 Cr editing of Account .
start_phrase: Amounts described in this Article 5 shall be credited to the Supplemental Account established for a Participant at such times and in such manner as may be determined by the Administrator .
summary:
- Transition/GE Capital transition contributions: At a Supplemental Distribution, only the vested portion (per the RSP) is payable; any non-vested portion is forfeited. The right to Transition Contributions expires when it does under the RSP; no Transition Contributions are made for periods after March 31, 2011.
- No disability contributions: Unlike the RSP, this Plan does not provide ongoing contributions due to disability.
- Company contributions for additional years of service (special agreements): The Company may, by special agreement, deem certain Participants to have five additional Years of Service under the RSP and credit an additional amount equal to up to 80% (or a lower agreed percentage) of base salary at hire (pre-deferral) for periods on/after January 1, 2008. Credits are calculated under Administrator procedures applied consistently, are generally subject to five-year vesting, and are forfeited upon termination before five years of actual service except in cases of death or RSP-defined disability. Amounts are credited to the Participant’s RSP-Related Account.
- Crediting of accounts (Section 5.3):
  - Timing/manner: Administrator determines; aims to align with Qualified Retirement Plans but is not required to do so.
  - Section 415 limitation make-up amounts for the RP are estimated at Separation from Service using consistent assumptions and credited immediately before Plan payments commence.
  - Special agreement (5.2(c)) credits are determined and credited on the one-year anniversary of the later of the special agreement date or employment start.
  - Company stock contributions (5.2(b)(i)) are credited to a Stock Fund subaccount consistent with Stock Fund practices.
  - Other contributions (profit-sharing, matching, conversion, GE Capital transition, and special agreement credits) are credited to RSP-Related Account subaccounts reflecting available RSP investment funds, subject to Stock Fund limits and redirection rules; no self-directed brokerage subaccount unless the Administrator permits.
  - The Administrator may establish additional book reserve accounts and set procedures for recognizing investment results.
- Supplemental benefits payment election (Section 5.4): Supplemental Benefits are paid in cash from the Company’s general assets in the form elected by the Participant. Existing Participants (including certain Prior SRP participants not in pay status as of December 31, 2004) may make elections under Administrator rules compliant with Section 409A.
text:
Section 5.3    Cr editing of Account .
(a)    Time and Manner . Amounts  described in this Article 5 shall be credited to the Supplemental Account established
for a Participant at such times and in such manner as may be determined by the Administrator . In making such credits, the
Administrator shall generally attempt to, but shall not be required to, credit accounts at a time and in a manner as similar as possible

Separation from Service, based on such assumptions as the Administrator may reasonably impose and consistently applied to
similarly situated Participants, and assuming that the Participant would begin receiving
-17-benefits under the RP at the time of the Participant’ s Separation from Service, or if later, at the earliest possible date that the

Plan; and
(ii)    unless otherw ise determined by the Administrator or agreed in a special agreement with a Participant,

title: Supplemental Benefits Payment Election
heading: Section 5.4 Suppl emental Benefits Payment Election .
start_phrase: Any Supplemental Benefits payable under the Plan shall be paid in cash from the general assets of the Company in the form elected by the Participant subject to the following:
summary:
- How and when supplemental retirement credits are posted:
  - Special agreement credits are generally determined and credited on the one‑year anniversary of the later of the special agreement date or employment start, with consistent procedures for similarly situated participants.
  - Company stock-related contributions are credited to an RSP‑Related Account in a Stock Fund subaccount, with amounts determined consistent with Stock Fund practices.
  - Other company contributions (profit-sharing, matching, conversion, GE Capital transition) and special agreement credits are credited to RSP‑Related Account subaccounts tied to available RSP investment funds, subject to limits on Stock Fund allocations and no self-directed brokerage subaccounts.
  - The Administrator may establish additional book reserve accounts and set procedures for reflecting gains, losses, interest, dividends, and other adjustments.

- Supplemental Benefits payment elections (Section 5.4) and Section 409A compliance:
  - Benefits are paid in cash from the company’s general assets, in a form elected by the participant.
  - Permissible forms: single lump sum or annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years (for amounts not subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election).
  - Transition rules for elections and modifications for participants around 2004–2005, including one-time changes by 12/31/2005 without the usual 5‑year additional deferral, as permitted by 409A transition guidance.
  - For participants first becoming eligible after 12/31/2005 (with detailed rules for those first eligible on/after 1/1/2012 or tied to Q4 2011 compensation):
    - Initial elections may not apply to certain early company contributions; those amounts default to an Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
    - Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election: default to a single lump-sum payable on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after the earliest of separation, disability, or death (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but within 90 days). This automatic election cannot be modified.
    - Contributions outside the automatic periods are governed by the participant’s initial election.
    - Rehired participants are treated as newly eligible for post‑rehire contributions for election purposes.
  - Default rule if no valid, timely election: single lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, disability, or death (or within 90 days thereafter).
  - One-time modification right (if not previously used) before separation: must comply with 409A (minimum five‑year additional deferral; effective 12 months after change). No changes allowed after separation. Rehired participants may use a new one‑time modification for post‑rehire elections.
  - Prior SRP Plan coordination, including exceptions for benefits already in pay status and non-reduction rules for certain pre‑2005 accelerations.

- Elective Deferrals eligibility and enrollment (Article 6):
  - Amex notifies eligible employees; erroneous notifications do not confer eligibility and related elections are void to the extent allowed by 409A.
  - Participation requires a timely Deferral Election; standard Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1.
  - Special 30‑day election window for employees first entering Band 50 (or first becoming eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan while in Band 50); eligibility starts the first payroll period after the 30‑day window. The Administrator may coordinate special and open enrollment and limit special enrollment when appropriate.
  - For non‑Band 50 employees who become eligible by exceeding the 401(a)(17) compensation limit:
    - If eligibility occurs in the first three quarters, participation begins the following January 1 via open enrollment.
    - If eligibility occurs in the fourth quarter, participation begins the first pay period after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following year.

Section 5.4    Suppl emental Benefits Payment Election . Any Supplemental Benefits payable under the Plan shall be paid in
cash from the general assets of the Company in the form elected by the Participant subject to the following:
(a)    In accordanc e with rules and procedures adopted by the Administrator in compliance with Section 409A,
existing Participants, including Participants (other than those in pay status on December 31, 2004) under the Prior SRP Plan, may
make Supplemental Elections as follows:
-18-(i)    Participants who have not previously made an initial Supplemental Election under Section 5.4(b),
whether under the Plan or under the Prior SRP Plan, may make such an initial Supplemental Election on or before the date set by the
Administrator , which shall not be later than December 31, 2005.
(ii)    Participants who have previously made an initial Supplemental Election under Section 5.4(b), whether
under the Plan or under the Prior SRP Plan, but who have not previously modifi ed such election under Section 5.4(d), whether under
the Plan or under the Prior SRP Plan, may change such Supplemental Election on or before the date set by the Administrator , which
shall not be later than December 31, 2005, to elect any payment form permissible under Section 5.4(b) and Section 409A, regardless
of whether such Supplemental Election lengthens or shortens the period over which payments from the Plan shall be made. For the
avoidance of doubt, any such distributio n which accelerates payments from the Plan shall not cause any reduction in the amounts
otherwise payable hereunder . Notwithstanding Section 5.4(d), if made on or before December 31, 2005 in accordance with this
Section 5.4(a)(ii), such subsequent Supplemental Election shall be made in accordance with Section 409A, but, to the extent
permitted under Section 409A  transition guidance, need not comply with the requirement regarding a minimum additional deferral
period of five years. Any such subsequent Supplemental Election made under this Section 5.4(a)(ii) shall constitute a modification
for purposes of the one-time limitation contained in Section 5.4(d), and no addit ional modification will thereafter be permitted under
Section 5.4(d).
(iii)    Employees who first become Participants after December 31, 2005 may make an initial Supplemental
Election in accordance with rules and procedures adopted by the Administra tor in compliance with Section 409A, which, with
respect to Employe es who first become Participants on or after January 1, 2012 and individuals who first become entitled to
Supplemental Benefits as a result of Compensation paid during the fourth quarte r of 2011 (by way of clarification, it is intended that
individuals included in an enrollment process attributable to the third quarter of 2011 or an earlier quarter will not be covered by this
rule, regar dless of whether such individ uals filed elections regarding Deferral Benefits and/or Supplemental Benefits at that time or
instead were made subject to a default election), shall be applied as follows:
(A)    A Participant’ s initial Supplemental Election shall not be effective with respect to Company
contributions described in the following paragraphs:
(i)    In the case of a Participant who first receives Compensation with respect to which
Company contributi ons are credited under this Plan for the first, second or third quarter of the calendar year, or in the case of a new
Participant in Band 50 or above, whose 30 day election period under Article 6 (or open enrollment period offered in lieu of a special
enrollment period) expires no later than December 31 of the Participant’ s first calendar year as a Band 50 Employee eligible to
participate in this Plan, or in the case of a new Participant who is not in Band 50 or above, who is permitted to file an election during
open enrollment under Article 6 for the following calendar year, such Parti cipant’ s initial Supplemental Election shall not be
effective with respect to Company contributions calculated based on Compensation paid prior to the end of the first calendar year
beginning on or after the date on which the Participant first is paid Compensation with respect to which Companyst
-19-contributions under this Plan are calculated, or in which the Participant is otherwise described in this paragraph.
(ii)    In the case of a Participant who first is paid Compensation with respect to which
Company contributions are calculated for the fourth quarter of a calendar year or who in the case of a new Participant in Band 50 or
above, has a 30 day election period under Article 6 expiring later than December 31st of the Participant’ s first calendar year as a
Band 50 Employee eligible to particip ate in this Plan and is not enrolled via the annual enrollment process in lieu of special
enrollment, or in the case of a new Participant who is not in Band 50 or above, who is not permitted to participate in open enrollment
under Article 6 for the following calendar year, such Participant’ s initial Supplemental Election shall not be effective with respect to
Company contributions calculated based  on Compensation paid prior to the end of the second calendar year beginning on or after the
date the Participant  is first paid Compensation with respect to which Company contributions are calculated, or in which the
Participant is otherwise described in this paragraph.
(iii)    For the avoidance of doubt, solely for the purposes of determining which Supplemental
Benefits are subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, a Participant with Compensation with respect to which
Supplemental Benefits could be calculated is considered for purposes of this subsection to have such Supplemental Benefits
calculated, regardless of whether the Participant actually qualifies for such Supplemental Benefits to be credited to the Participant’ s
Account. For example, a Participant’ s failure to satisfy the service requirement or make contributions required to receive Company
Matching Contributi ons, or the Compan y’s decision not to make contributions,  shall not impact the duration of the Automatic New
Participant Supplemental Election.
(B)    Instead, with respect to Company  contributions not covered by the Participant’ s Supplemental
Election, the Company shall be deemed  to have made an Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election for the Participant (or
his or her beneficia ry, in the event of the Participant’ s death) to receive his or her Supplemental Benefits attributable to such
contributions in the form of a single lump sum as of the January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months following the earliest of his or
her Separa tion from  Service or the date of Disability or death, as applicable (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter , but in
any event no later than 90 days).
(C)    Company contributions that are not subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental
Election by reason of being calculated with respect to Compensation paid later than the time periods set forth in Section 5.4(a)(iii)
(A) above shall be subject to a Participant’ s initial Supplemental Election.
(D)    With respect to an Employee who was a former Participant and again becomes a Participant after
being rehired by the Company followin g his or her Separation from Service, the election rules in this Section shall apply to the
Company Matching  Contributions, Company Conversion Contributions and Company Profit-Sharing Contributions made to such
Participant followin g his or her rehire date as if the rehire date (or if later, the resumption of eligibility to participate) were the date
of initial participation eligibility .
-20-(iv)    Participants who have previously made both a Supplemental Electio n and a modification to such
Supplemental Electi on shall be subject to the rules of Section 5.4(d) prohibiting  any further changes to their Supplemental Elections.
However , any Participant who was not in pay status (as defined in Section 1.1(c)) on January 1, 2005 and who previously made a
modification to an initial Supplemental Election which accelerated the time period for payments from the Plan shall not have any
reduction in the amounts otherwise payable hereunder (notwithstanding Section V(D)(1)(b)(ii) of the Prior SRP  Plan).
(b)    A Participant may elect to receive his or her Supplemental Benefits that are not covered by the Automatic New
Participant Supplemental Election in a single lump-sum payment or in annual installments payable over a period of five, ten or 15
consecutive calenda r years. Except as provided in Section 5.4(d), a Participant may not modify his or her initial Supplemental
Election described in the preceding sente nce. Such subsequent Supplemental Election shall apply to the payment of all Supplemental
Benefits under the Plan and the Prior SRP Plan that are not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election
(except for benefits that were in pay status on December 31, 2004). A Participant’ s reemployment after Separation from Service shall
not affect benefits attributable to periods prior to his or her Separation from Service, and he or she shall be subject to a new
Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and initial Supplemental Election with respect to post-reemployment benefits.
(c)    If a Participan t fails to make a valid, timely Supplemental Election in accordance with Section 5.4(a) and the
rules and procedures adopted by the Administrator , such Participant shall be deemed to have made an initial Supplemental Election
to receive his or her Supplemental Benefits that are not covered by the Autom atic New Participant Supplemental Election in the
form of a single lump sum as of the January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months following the earliest of his or her Separation from
Service or the date of Disability or death, as applicable (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter , but in any event no later
than 90 days).
(d)    A Participant who has not previously modified an initial Supplemental Election may make a one-time
modification to his or her initial Supplemental Election to elect a different form of payment for Supplemental Benefits under the
Plan that are not covered by the Autom atic New Participant Supplemental Election. To be effective, such a modification shall be
made by filing a written notice of modification in such form and manner as the Administrator may prescribe; provided, however , that
the modifi cation must comply with Section 409A, including the requirements regarding: (i) a minimum additional deferral period of
five years,  and (ii) the subsequent Supplemental Election not being effective until 12 months after it is made. A Participant may not
change the payment method of his or her Supplemental Benefits after his or her Separation from Service. Notwithstanding the
previous sentence, with respect to an Employee who was a former Participant and again becomes a Participant after being rehired by
the Company following his or her Separation from Service, the one-time modification under this Section 5.4(d) shall be permitted
with respect to such Participant’ s initia l Supplemental Election made following his or her rehire date, regardless of whether the
Participant had also made such a modification for benefits earned prior to Separation from Service. By way of clarification, the
Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election cannot be modified.

title: Notification
heading: Section 6.1 Notifi cation .
start_phrase: Employees eligible to participate in the Plan for a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits will be notified by Amex of their eligibility to participate for such Plan Year.
summary:
- Article 6 covers Elective Deferrals: how eligibility is communicated, who can participate each Plan Year, when elections can be made, and when eligibility starts.
- Section 6.1 (Notification): Amex notifies employees of eligibility. An erroneous notice does not create eligibility; any deferral election by an ineligible person is void to the extent permitted under Section 409A.
- Section 6.2 (Participation): 
  - An employee becomes a Participant for Deferral Benefits in a Plan Year by making a Deferral Election under Section 6.5 if they:
    - Were a Participant in the prior Plan Year as of the Band 50 Determination Date, or
    - Are employed in Band 50 or above as of that prior-year Band 50 Determination Date, or
    - Become Band 50 or above (or first become eligible while Band 50 or above) before the end of the prior Plan Year and are authorized to enroll.
  - Standard Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1 of the Plan Year.
  - Special rules (per Section 6.3):
    - (a) New to Plan and in Band 50+ (or become eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan while remaining Band 50+): may file an election within 30 days of becoming eligible; Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is the first payroll period after that 30-day window. The Administrator may coordinate special and open enrollments and limit special enrollment when appropriate.
    - (b) Not in Band 50+; eligibility triggered by exceeding the IRC Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit:
      - If the limit is first exceeded in the first three quarters: eligible January 1 of the following Plan Year and may enroll during open enrollment.
      - If first exceeded in the final calendar quarter: eligible as of the first pay period beginning after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following year.
text:
Section 6.1    Notifi cation . Employees eligible to participate in the Plan for a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits will
be notified by Amex  of their eligibility to participate for such Plan Year. If Amex erroneously notifies an individual of his or her
eligibility to participate, and such indivi dual does not meet the requirements of Section 4.2 or such individual has been excluded by
the Administrator pursuant to Section 4.1, such erroneous notification shall not cause the individual to be eligible, and any Deferral
Election made by such ineligible individual shall be null and void and of no ef fect to the extent permissible under Section 409A.

title: Participation
heading: Section 6.2 Participation .
start_phrase: An eligible Employee for a Plan Year who was a Participant in the prior Plan Year as of the Band 50 Determinat ion Date, or who is employed in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date in the prior Plan Year, or who otherwise becomes employed in Band 50 or above or first becomes eligible while in Band 50 or above prior to the end of the prior Plan Year and is authorized by the Administrator to participate in enrollme nt shall become a Participant in the Plan with respect to Deferra l Benefits for such Plan Year by making a Deferral Election in accordance with Section 6.5 for the Plan Year.
summary:
- Article 6 governs Elective Deferrals, detailing eligibility notifications, participation rules, special enrollment timing, and 409A compliance.
- Section 6.1 (Notification): Amex notifies eligible employees each Plan Year; erroneous notices do not confer eligibility. Any deferral election by an ineligible individual is void to the extent allowed under Section 409A.
- Section 6.2 (Participation):
  - Who can participate: Employees who were prior-year Participants as of the Band 50 Determination Date, are Band 50+ as of that date, or who become Band 50+ (or otherwise first become eligible while Band 50+) before the end of the prior Plan Year and are authorized to enroll. Participation is by making a Deferral Election (per Section 6.5). Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1 of the Plan Year.
  - Special rules:
    - (a) New Band 50+ entrants (or those in Band 50+ who newly become eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan) may file an election within 30 days; eligibility begins the first payroll period after that 30-day window. The Administrator may coordinate or limit special enrollment near year-end.
    - (b) Employees not in Band 50+ who first become eligible by exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit:
      - If this occurs in the first three quarters, eligibility begins January 1 of the following Plan Year (open enrollment applies).
      - If it occurs in the final quarter, eligibility begins the first pay period after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following Plan Year; advance elections allowed by the Administrator’s deadline in accordance with Section 6.3.
      - Clarifications: Exceeding the Section 415 limit alone does not create special enrollment; the date of exceeding 401(a)(17) is based on Plan Year Compensation even if some pay is excluded from Supplemental Benefits due to unfulfilled service requirements.
    - (c) Mid-year elections are generally prohibited unless expressly permitted and compliant with Section 6.3; must meet Administrator deadlines. All Deferral Elections become irrevocable by the day before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date (or earlier if set by the Administrator).
- Section 6.3 (Newly Eligible Employees): Consistent with Section 409A and Section 6.2, mid-year enrollment may be offered to employees who newly become eligible and were not previously eligible for an Amex elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement. Employees previously eligible may still be treated as newly eligible (and allowed mid-year enrollment) if either:
  - (a) They received full payout of all prior elective account-balance amounts and were not eligible to continue participation at the time of the last payment (ignoring any right to delay payment); or
  - (b) They had ceased eligibility under all such plans and were not eligible at any time during the preceding 24 months before re-eligibility (ignoring mere rights to accrue earnings), regardless of whether prior deferrals have been paid.
- Section 6.4 (Deferrable Compensation): Introduces “Eligible Compensation,” but the substantive content is not included in the excerpt.

title: Newly Eligible Employees
heading: Section 6.3 Newl y Eligible Employees .
start_phrase: To the extent perm issible under Section 409A and Section 6.2, Employees who become eligible to participate in the Plan during a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits and who have not previously been eligible to participate in an elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement (as defined for purposes of Section 409A) of Amex or its subsidiaries may be offered by Amex the opportunity to participate in the Plan for the Plan Year in accordance with Section 6.2.
summary:
- Sets rules for timing and irrevocability of deferral elections: employees may elect before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date (first day of the relevant pay period) by the Administrator’s deadline; elections become irrevocable no later than the day before that date (or an earlier Administrator-set date).
- Clarifies no special mid-year enrollment right arises merely because an employee exceeds the Internal Revenue Code Section 415 limit under a qualified plan.
- Clarifies that the date an employee exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit is based on total Plan Year compensation, even if some compensation is excluded from supplemental benefits due to unmet service requirements for company contributions.
- Generally prohibits mid-year elections; any permitted mid-year election must also satisfy Section 6.3 and be filed by the Administrator’s deadline.
- Defines “Newly Eligible Employees” under Section 6.3 consistent with Section 409A and Section 6.2:
  - Employees newly eligible during a Plan Year who were not previously eligible for an Amex elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement may be offered participation for that year.
  - Employees previously eligible may be treated as newly eligible (and allowed mid-year enrollment) if either:
    - They received all payments from this and any other elective account-balance plan and, at the last payment date, were not eligible to continue participation (ignoring any payment delay rights), or
    - They ceased eligibility and were not eligible to participate in any such plan at any time during the prior 24 months before re-eligibility (ignoring earnings accrual rights), regardless of whether prior deferrals have been paid.
- Introduces Section 6.4 on Deferrable Compensation, beginning with “Eligible Compensation” (details not included in the excerpt).

Section 6.3    Newl y Eligible Employees . To the extent perm issible under Section 409A  and Section 6.2, Employees who
become eligible to participate in the Plan during a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits and who have not previously been
eligible to participate in an elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement (as defined for purposes of Section 409A)

or any other elective account-balance plan, disregarding for this purpose any right to delay payment; or
(b)    The Employee  had ceased to be eligible to participate in Deferral Benefit s under the Plan and all other elective

title: Deferrable Compensation
heading: Section 6.4 Deferrable Compensation .
start_phrase: An eligible Employee for a Plan Year may elect to defer a specified amount from one or more of the following items:
summary:
- Clarifies mid-year deferral elections: generally prohibited except as expressly permitted under Sections 6.2 and 6.3; any permitted mid-year election must meet Section 6.3 requirements, be filed by the Administrator’s deadline, and becomes irrevocable as of the day before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date (or earlier if set by the Administrator).
- Provides clarifications on statutory limits: no special enrollment right arises from exceeding the Section 415 limit; the date an Employee exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit is determined on Plan Year Compensation, even if some compensation is excluded from supplemental benefit calculations due to service requirements.
- Defines when “newly eligible” mid-year participation is allowed under Section 409A: 
  - Employees not previously eligible for an Amex elective account-balance deferred compensation plan may be offered participation mid-year.
  - Previously eligible Employees may be treated as newly eligible if (a) they received full payout of all elective account-balance plans and were not eligible to continue at the last payment date, or (b) they had ceased eligibility and were not eligible under any such plan for at least 24 months before re-eligibility (ignoring rights to delay payment or to accrue earnings).
- Specifies deferrable compensation:
  - Standard elections may include Base Salary for the Plan Year and Incentive Pay payable in the second Plan Year after the election (excluding amounts earned before the start of the Plan Year following the filing).
  - Mid-year/newly eligible elections may include Base Salary for payroll periods beginning on/after the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date and a prorated portion of Incentive Pay payable in the following Plan Year based on days remaining in the year or performance period.
- Sets maximum deferral limits and methodology:
  - Administrator imposes limits and may waive them before the election becomes effective.
  - Aggregate deferrals from Base Salary (next Plan Year) and Incentive Pay (second following Plan Year) are capped by reference to 100% of a specified Base Salary rate as of set dates, with special rules for mid-year eligibility due to Band 50 status or exceeding the 401(a)(17) limit.
  - Provides a formula to cap Incentive Pay deferral based on the remaining percentage after the Base Salary deferral election.
  - Deferrals cannot exceed net cash amounts after withholdings.
  - Administrator may set stricter caps (current default maximum of 85% of Incentive Pay).
- Outlines computation methods: Administrator may require elections as percentages, dollar amounts, or other reasonable methods; may allow multiple methods; may let elections apply only to compensation above the Section 401(a)(17) limit.
- Details deferral election procedures:
  - Timing: generally due by December 15 of the preceding Plan Year (or the next Monday if Dec 15 falls on a weekend), with separate deadlines for permitted mid-year elections.
  - Form: as prescribed by the Administrator.
  - Contents: must specify the compensation items and amounts within plan limits; includes additional provisions for Band 50 employees (text continues beyond the excerpt).

title: Deferral Benefits Election
heading: Section 6.5 Deferral Benefits Election .
start_phrase: An eligible Emplo yee for a Plan Year who wants to participate in the Plan with respect to Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year must make an irrevocable Deferral Election for the Plan Year on or before the December 15 of the preceding Plan Year, or if December 15 is on a weekend, the following Monday , or as of such other deadline as the Administrator may establish (but in all events prior to the beginning of such Plan Year);
summary:
- Sets limits on Deferral Elections:
  - Deferrals cannot exceed amounts otherwise payable in cash, net of applicable withholdings.
  - The Administrator may impose additional limits on deferral amounts/percentages before elections take effect; by default, up to 85% of Incentive Pay may be deferred.
  - Clarifies that actual Base Salary paid may change the dollar amount deferred but does not change the maximum Incentive Pay limit tied to prior periods.

- Defines how deferral amounts can be computed:
  - Elections may be stated as percentages or dollar amounts of Base Salary and/or Incentive Pay, or via another reasonable method selected by the Administrator.
  - The Administrator may allow multiple calculation methods or require one.
  - Elections may apply only to compensation above the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation.

- Establishes timing and process for Deferral Benefits Elections (Section 6.5):
  - Elections are irrevocable and generally must be made by December 15 of the preceding Plan Year (or the next Monday if that date falls on a weekend), and in all cases before the Plan Year begins.
  - Mid‑year eligibility allows a later deadline per Section 6.2, or an earlier Administrator‑set deadline.
  - Elections must be made in the form and by the deadlines the Administrator prescribes.

- Specifies required election content:
  - The compensation items to defer (eligible under Section 6.4(a)) and the amount of each, subject to Section 6.4(b) and any administrative limits.

- Provides special time and form of payment elections for Band 50 and above:
  - Eligible Band 50 Employees may elect payment timing: either upon Separation from Service or on a specified date at least five years after the last day of the Plan Year.
  - They may elect payment form: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years.
  - Default if no valid time and form are elected: lump‑sum payment on the January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months after Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but no later than 90 days).
  - Employees below Band 50 cannot make special time/form elections; their Deferral Benefits follow the Supplemental Election under Section 5.4. Newly hired/promoted/transferred Band 50 employees may be allowed to participate in open enrollment for the following Plan Year.

- Details withholding mechanics:
  - Base Salary deferrals are withheld from each regular payroll.
  - Incentive Pay deferrals are withheld when the Incentive Pay is (or would be) paid.

- Addresses crediting and accounts:
  - The Administrator maintains a Deferral Account for each Participant’s Deferral Benefits and may use subaccounts to track earnings/losses per Article 7.
  - Article 7 earnings: each Participant’s RP‑Related Account (per Section 5.1) is credited not less than annually with Imputed Earnings Credits, at the same interest rate and in a similar manner as under the RP.

Section 6.5    Deferral Benefits Election .
(a)    Time of Deferral Election . An eligible Emplo yee for a Plan Year who wants to participate in the Plan with
respect to Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year must make an irrevocable Deferral Election for the Plan Year on or before the December
15 of the preceding Plan Year, or if December 15 is on a weekend, the following Monday , or as of such other deadline as the
Administrator may establish (but in all events prior to the beginning of such Plan Year); provided, however , that an Employee
permitted under Section 6.2 to make a mid-year Deferral Election for the Plan Year in which he or she becomes eligible to
participate may make a Deferral Electi on by the deadline established under that Section (or by such earlier deadline as may be
established by the Administrator).
(b)    Form of Deferral Election . A Deferral Election for a Plan Year shall be made in the manner and by the deadlines
prescribed by the Administrator .
(c)    Contents of Deferral Election . In his or her Deferral Election for a Plan Year, the Employee shall specify:
(i)    the items of his or her compensatio n eligible for deferral under Section 6.4(a) that the Employee wishes
to defer for the Plan Year and the amount of each such item to be deferred, provided that the amount of all items to be deferred
complies with Section 6.4(b) and any administrative limits imposed on elections made for such Plan Year;
(ii)    in the case of an Employee in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date in the prior Plan
Year (or a non-Participant who first becomes an eligible Band 50 Employee after such date and is permitted by the Administrator to
participate in open enrollment for the following Plan Year on account of such hire or promotion into Band 50):
-25-(A)    the time when his or her Deferral Benefits for such Plan Year shall be paid, which shall be either
(A) the Separation from Service of the Participant, or (B) a specified date at least five years after the last day of the Plan Year at the
time of the election; and
(B)    the form of payment of his or her Deferral Benefits for the Plan Year, which shall be (A) a lump
sum, or (B) five, ten or 15 substantially equal annual installments.
In the event that an Employee’ s Deferral Election pursuant to Section 6.5(a) and Section 6.5(b), does not specify both a valid
time of payment pursuant to Section 6.5(c)(ii)(A) and a valid form of payment pursuant to Section 6.5(c)(ii)(B), such Employee shall
be deemed to have elected a lump-sum payment as of the January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months following his or her
Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter , but in any event no later than 90 days).
By way of clarificati on, an Employee who is not in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date for the prior Plan
Year may not file a special election regarding time and form of payment for Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year. Instead, the
Supplemental Election (without regard to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election) made pursuant to Section 5.4 will
also apply  to such Deferral Benefits. However , as set forth above, in the case of a new Participant who is enrolled as a result of being
hired into or promo ted to Band 50 (or transferring to eligible status while in Band 50 or above) after such date, the Administrator
may permit such Employee to participate in open enrollment for the following Plan Year as a Band 50 or above Employee.
(d)    Withholding of Amounts Deferred . For each Plan Year, the Base Salary portion of a Participant’ s Deferral
Election shall be withheld from each regularly scheduled Base Salary payro ll, and the Incentive Pay portion of a Participant’ s
Deferral Election shall be withheld at the time the Incentive Pay is or otherwise would be paid to the Participant.

title: Crediting of Deferred Amounts
heading: Section 6.6 Crediting of Deferr ed Amounts .
start_phrase: The Administrator shall establish and maintain a Deferral Account with respect to each Participant’ s Deferral Benefits.
summary:
- Participants must elect both the time and form of payment for each Plan Year’s Deferral Benefits:
  - Time: either upon Separation from Service or a specified date at least five years after the end of the Plan Year.
  - Form: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years.
- Default rule if a valid time and form are not both elected: payment will be a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but no later than 90 days).
- Eligibility clarification on special elections:
  - Employees below Band 50 as of the prior Plan Year’s Band 50 Determination Date cannot make a special time/form election; the Supplemental Election under Section 5.4 applies.
  - New Participants who become Band 50 (by hire, promotion, or transfer) after that date may be allowed to participate in the next open enrollment as Band 50 or above.
- Withholding of deferrals:
  - Base Salary deferrals are withheld from each regular payroll.
  - Incentive Pay deferrals are withheld when the incentive is or would be paid.
- Crediting of deferrals:
  - The Administrator establishes a Deferral Account for each Participant and credits deferred amounts at times and in manners it determines.
  - Accounts may be divided into subaccounts to track earnings and losses per Article 7.
- Earnings (Article 7):
  - Each Participant’s RP-Related Account is credited, at least annually, with Imputed Earnings Credits (as defined in the RP), using the same interest rate and similar computation method as under the RP, under procedures and timing set by the Administrator and applied consistently to similarly situated Participants.

title: RSP-Related Account
heading: Section 7.2 RSP -Related Account .
start_phrase: A Partic ipant’ s RSP-Related Account shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below .
summary:
- Section 7.2 establishes that a Participant’s RSP-Related Account is credited with earnings using the Hypothetical Investment Method.
- Section 7.3 (Deferral Accounts) sets how Deferral Benefits earn returns by role and time period:
  - (a) For Plan Year 2011 and later, Deferral Benefits earn under the Hypothetical Investment Method; 2010 Incentive Pay paid in 2011 is treated as 2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - (b) Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings credited in Plan Years beginning on/after January 1, 2011 use the Hypothetical Investment Method; earnings credited in 2010 and prior use the Interest Method. 2010 earnings (not paid by October 27, 2010) are capped at the AFR if Amex’s ROE is below the target range; amounts paid before October 27, 2010 used the Interest Method without the AFR cap.
  - (c) Non-Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through December 31, 2011. If a Participant becomes an Executive Officer during 2011, 2011 earnings on pre-2011 benefits are capped at the AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR). From 2012 onward, the Hypothetical Investment Method applies.
  - (d) Retirees: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through December 31, 2012; the Hypothetical Investment Method applies effective January 1, 2013.
- Section 7.4 (Hypothetical Investment Method) allows Participants to direct credits among subaccounts described in Section 5.3. For Deferral Benefits from pre-2011 Plan Years, Participants may elect an option crediting earnings at the AFR instead of the Stock Fund or RSP-based options.
- Company Stock limits: transfers to the Stock Fund are prohibited if they would cause Company Stock to exceed 10% of the value of the relevant Deferral Account or RSP-Related Account at the time of transfer; there is also a cap of no more than 10% of new contributions directed to the Stock Fund (sentence truncated in the excerpt).
