title: Hypothetical Investment Method
heading: Section 7.4 Hypothetical Investment Method .
start_phrase: For each Participant, credits to his or her RSP-Related and Deferral Account (to the extent subject to the Hypothetical Investment Method) shall be made to such subaccounts thereunder as directed by such Participant, using the subaccounts described in Section 5.3,
summary:
- Establishes how earnings are credited to Participants’ RSP-Related and Deferral Accounts, primarily via the Hypothetical Investment Method, with specific transition rules from the Interest Method based on participant status and plan years.
- Section 7.2: RSP-Related Accounts always earn under the Hypothetical Investment Method.
- Section 7.3 (Deferral Accounts):
  - 2011 and later Plan Years: Deferral Benefits earn under the Hypothetical Investment Method. 2010 Incentive Pay paid in 2011 and deferred is treated as 2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings credited in Plan Years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2011 use the Hypothetical Investment Method; earnings credited in 2010 and prior Plan Years use the Interest Method. 2010 earnings (not paid by Oct 27, 2010) are capped at AFR if Amex’s ROE is below target; amounts paid before Oct 27, 2010 used the Interest Method without the AFR cap.
  - Non-Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through Dec 31, 2011; if the participant becomes an Executive Officer during 2011, 2011 earnings on pre-2011 Deferral Benefits are capped at AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR before becoming an Executive Officer). From 2012 forward, the Hypothetical Investment Method applies.
  - Retirees: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through Dec 31, 2012; the Hypothetical Investment Method applies beginning Jan 1, 2013.
- Section 7.4 (Hypothetical Investment Method mechanics):
  - Participants allocate credits among subaccounts (per RSP investment options), in 1% increments, with change frequency generally mirroring RSP rules and any additional plan rules.
  - For pre-2011 Deferral Benefits, a Participant may elect an AFR-based option instead of the Stock Fund or RSP-based options.
  - Stock Fund concentration limits: no transfers or new contributions that would cause Company Stock holdings in either the Deferral Account or RSP-Related Account to exceed 10% of that Account’s total value; no more than 10% of new contributions to either Account may be directed to the Stock Fund. Any excess is redirected to the Plan’s default fund.
  - Subaccounts track the actual performance (dividends, gains/losses) of the elected funds (or AFR, if chosen). Transfers among funds follow RSP-like rules, subject to Plan-specific limits and Administrator rules. Failure to elect results in investment in an Administrator-selected default fund (generally the RSP default), and the Administrator may exclude certain RSP funds (including any self-directed brokerage) from availability.
  - Valuation follows uniform Administrator rules aiming to mirror timing and market factors used in the RSP.
- Section 7.5 (Interest Method for applicable Deferral Accounts):
  - Annual crediting at the applicable Schedule Rate, subject to plan limits.
  - Vesting: principal is always 100% vested. Until Jan 1, 2011, earnings at the Minimum Schedule Rate vest as credited; earnings above the Minimum Schedule Rate vest upon Retirement Eligibility, or earlier death/Disability. Effective Dec 31, 2010, all unpaid Interest Method earnings became fully vested.
- Section 7.6 (Special Restrictions for Insiders):
  - Applies to Insiders while they are Insiders and during any post-cessation period requiring reporting under Exchange Act Rule 16a-2(b); ceases when Insider status (and any such period) ends. Begins automatically when a Participant becomes an Insider.
  - Imposes additional limits on Insider investment credits and transfers (text partially truncated), intended to restrict certain subaccount allocations, especially those tied to Company Stock.

Section 7.4    Hypothetical Investment Method .
(a)    For each Participant, credits to his or her RSP-Related and Deferral Account (to the extent subject to the
Hypothetical Investment Method) shall be made to such subaccounts thereunder as directed by such Participant, using the
subaccounts described in Section 5.3, provided, however , that with respect to Deferral Benefits attributable to Plan Years prior to
2011, the Participant may elect to have all or some of such Deferral Benefits invested in an investment option that credits earnings at
the AFR instead of in the Stock Fund or the RSP-based investment options, and provided further that no Participant may transfer
amounts to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund to the extent that such transfer would result in the aggregate Company Stock
holdings of such Participant under the Plan exceeding ten percent of (i) the total value of his or her Deferral Account (determined at
the time of the transfer) with respect to the investment of the Deferral Account or (ii) the total value of his or her RSP-Related
Account (determined at the time of the transfer) with respect to the investment  of the RSP-Related Account, nor may a Participant
direct that more than ten percent of new contributions
-27-made to the RSP-Re lated Account or the Deferral Account, respectively , be directed to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund.
If more than one subaccount is available, a Participant must designate, on a form or other medium acceptable to the Administrator , in
one-percent increme nts, the amounts to be credited to each subaccount. A Participant shall be allowed to amend such designation
consistent with the frequency of investment changes offered the Participant under rules governing the RSP for a given Plan Year,
subject to any different or additional rules as may be established by the Administrator for this Plan. If a Participant has directed the
transfer of amounts to the Stock Fund and the credits to the relevant Account of a Participant to the subaccount relating to the Stock
Fund would result in the aggregate Company Stock holdings of such Participant under the Plan exceeding ten percent of the total
value of such Account (determined at the time of the transfer) or has directed new contributions to an Account to the Stock Fund in
an amount which would result in new contributions to such Account’ s subaccount representing the Stock Fund exceeding ten percent
of new contributions to such Account, then such Participant shall be deemed to have selected, with respect to any such excess, the
default subaccount designated by the Administrator (which shall be deemed to be the subaccount representing the fund designated as
the default fund under the RSP , unless the Administrator directs the use of a dif ferent fund).
(b)    To the extent a Participant elects to invest in the subaccount representing the Stock Fund, subject to
Section 7.4(d) and Section 7.6, the limit on such investments set forth above, and such rules as may be adopted by the Administrator ,
the performance of the book reserve subaccount established for each Participant pursuant to Section 5.3 or Section 6.6 shall reflect
the perform ance of the Stock Fund. Such subaccount shall reflect such increas es or decreases in value from time to time, whether
from dividends, gains, losses or otherwise, as may be experienced by the Stock Fund. Subject to Section 7.6 and to such rules as may
be adopted  by the Administrator , a Participant may elect to transfer credits among the Stock Fund and one or more subaccounts
representing other investment options in a manner similar to the rules for such transfers under the RSP and such different or
additional rules as the Administrator may establish for this Plan; provided, however , no Participant may transfer amounts to the
subaccount representing the Stock Fund to the extent that such transfer would violate a limit on such investment established by the
Plan or the Administrator .
(c)    To the extent the Participant does not elect (or is not permitted) to invest in the subaccount representing the
Stock Fund, subject to Section 7.4(d), and to such rules as may be adopted by the Administrator , the performance of each book
reserve subaccount established for each Participant shall reflect the performance of the investment fund that the Participant elects to
have such subaccount represent. Each such subaccount shall reflect such increa ses or decreases in value from time to time, whether
from dividends, gains, losses or otherw ise, as that experienced by the related investment fund under the RSP or, in the case of the
AFR inves tment option, as indicated by the AFR. Subject to Section 7.6, credits  to such subaccounts may be transferred to any other
subaccount under the Plan in a manner  similar to the rules for such transfers under the RSP, on such terms and at such times as
permitted with respect to the related investment funds under the RSP and such similar rules as may be established for the AFR
option, subject in each case to such rules as may be adopted by the Administrator for this Plan. If a Participant fails to affirmatively
designate one or more subaccounts pursuant to this Section 7.4(c), subject to rules established by the Administrator , such Participant
shall be
-28-deemed to have selected a default accou nt selected by the Administrator (which shall be deemed to be the subaccount representing
the fund designated as the default fund under the RSP, unless the Administrator  directs the use of a different fund). Notwithstanding
the forego ing, the Administrator may, in its sole discretion, provide that one or more investment funds available under the RSP,
including any self-directed brokerage account which may be available under the RSP, shall not be available for designation under the
Plan.
(d)    The subaccounts shall be valued subject to such reasonable rules and procedures as the Administrator may adopt
and apply  to all Participants similarly situated with an effort to value such subaccounts as if amounts designated were invested at
similar times and in manners, subject to administrative convenience, as amounts are invested, and subject to the same market
fluctuation factors used in valuing such investments in the RSP .

title: Interest Method
heading: Section 7.5 Inter est Method .
start_phrase: (a) Under the Interest Method, a Participant’ s Deferral Account for a Plan Year shall be credited with interest equivalents each calendar year at the Schedule Rate in effect for the calendar year, subject to any limitations established under the Plan.
summary:
- Default investment designation: If a participant does not make an investment election, the Administrator will direct amounts to a default subaccount (generally the RSP’s default fund unless otherwise directed). The Administrator may exclude one or more RSP investment options, including any self-directed brokerage account, from being available under this Plan.
- Subaccount valuation: The Administrator will value subaccounts under uniform, reasonable rules intended to mirror the timing, manner, and market fluctuation factors used for comparable investments in the RSP, subject to administrative practicality.
- Interest Method (Section 7.5):
  - Crediting: Deferral Accounts using the Interest Method are credited annually with interest equivalents at the applicable Schedule Rate, subject to Plan limits.
  - Vesting:
    - Principal: Always 100% vested.
    - Earnings before 1/1/2011: Earnings at the Minimum Schedule Rate vest as credited; earnings above the Minimum Schedule Rate vest upon Retirement Eligibility or earlier death or Disability, and thereafter as credited.
    - Effective 12/31/2010: All unpaid earnings under the Interest Method become fully vested.
- Special Restrictions for Insiders (Section 7.6):
  - Applicability: Applies during any period a participant is an Insider, including post-cessation reporting periods under Exchange Act Rule 16a-2(b); automatically applies upon becoming an Insider and ceases after Insider status and any required reporting period end.
  - Funding restrictions: Credits to an Insider’s Account may not be directed to certain subaccounts (text truncated, but indicates limitations on where Insiders’ credits can be invested).

Section 7.5    Inter est Method . With respect to Deferral Accounts governed by the Interest Method:
(a)    Under the Interest Method, a Participant’ s Deferral Account for a Plan Year shall be credited with interest
equivalents each calendar year at the Schedule Rate in effect for the calendar year, subject to any limitations established under the
Plan.
(b)    The amounts in such Deferral Account shall vest as follows:
(i)    Principal . The principal amou nt of a Participant’ s Deferral Account for a Plan Year shall be 100 percent
vested at all times.
(ii)    Earnings . Until January 1, 2011, with respect to amounts credited with earnings unde r the Interest
Method, the earning s on a Participant’ s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year for a given calendar year at the Minimum Schedule Rate
for the calendar year shall be 100 percent vested as such earnings are accrued and credited, and the portion of the earnings on a
Participant’ s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year for a given calendar year at the applicable Schedule Rate in excess of the Minimum
Schedule Rate for the calendar year, if any, shall become vested on the date that the Participant becomes Retirement Eligible, or
upon the earlier death or Disability of the Participant, and thereafter as such earnings are accrued and credited. Effective December
31, 2010, all earnings amounts under the Interest Method with respect to Deferral Benefits not yet paid out shall be fully vested.

title: Special Restrictions
heading: Section 7.6 Special Restrictions .
start_phrase: (a) The provisions of this Section 7.6 shall apply to Insiders.
summary:
- Investment fund designations and valuation:
  - If a participant does not choose an investment option, amounts default to the Administrator-selected subaccount, typically the RSP’s default fund.
  - The Administrator may exclude certain RSP funds (including any self-directed brokerage account) from being available under the Plan.
  - Subaccounts are valued under uniform rules intended to mirror timing, manner, and market fluctuation factors used for comparable RSP investments, subject to administrative practicality.

- Interest Method for Deferral Accounts (Section 7.5):
  - Accounts earn interest equivalents each calendar year at the applicable Schedule Rate, subject to Plan limits.
  - Vesting:
    - Principal is always 100% vested.
    - Earnings before January 1, 2011: amounts up to the Minimum Schedule Rate vest as credited; earnings above that rate vest upon Retirement Eligibility or earlier death/disability.
    - Effective December 31, 2010: all Interest Method earnings on unpaid Deferral Benefits become fully vested.

- Special restrictions for Insiders (Section 7.6):
  - Apply while an individual is an Insider and during any required post-cessation reporting period under Rule 16a-2(b).
  - Restrictions:
    - No credits to a Stock Fund subaccount for Insiders.
    - No transfers into a Stock Fund subaccount at any time.
    - Credits (including any made pre-Insider status to a Stock Fund subaccount) cannot be transferred, withdrawn, paid, or otherwise changed except:
      - As per the participant’s payment election or death distribution rules, but only when permitted by securities laws (with any delay limited to what those laws require and consistent with Section 409A).
      - Under applicable Plan forfeiture provisions.
  - The Plan intends these provisions to qualify for the Rule 16b-3(d) exemption from Exchange Act Section 16; the Administrator will administer accordingly.

- Payment of Supplemental Benefits (Article 8, Section 8.1; excluding death/disability):
  - Rules apply separately to amounts under the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and other Supplemental Elections, if they differ.
  - Timing:
    - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (other than death/disability), within an administrative window not exceeding 90 days.
    - Installments: begin July 1 of the calendar year following Separation from Service (other than death/disability), within 90 days, and continue each July 1 (within 90 days) for the elected period.
  - Re-employment does not alter ongoing payment schedules established at Separation from Service.
  - If a one-time modification to the initial Supplemental Election (per Section 5.4(a)(ii) or 5.4(d)) is effective before Separation from Service, payments follow the modified election.
text:
Section 7.6    Special Restrictions .
(a)    The provisions of this Section 7.6 shall apply to Insiders. Such provisions shall apply during all periods that such
Participants are Insiders, including any period following cessation of Insider status during which such Participants are required to
report transactions pursuant to Rule 16a-2(b) (or its successor) under the Exchange Act. This Section 7.6 shall be automatically
applicable to any Participant who, on and after the date hereof, becomes an Insider. For purposes of the foregoing, the effective date
of this Section 7.6 shall be the date the Participant becomes an Insider . At such time as any Participant ceases to be an Insider (and
any period contemplated by Rule 16a-2(b) has expired), this Section 7.6 shall cease to be applicable to such Participant.
(b)    Notwithstanding anything in the Plan to the contrary , (i) except as set forth below , credits to the Account of an
Insider may not be made to a subaccount that reflects the
-29-performance of the Stock Fund, (ii) credits made to the Account of an Insider at any time may not be transferred to a subaccount that
reflects the performance of the Stock Fund and (iii) credits made to an Insider ’s Account at any time, and credits to a subaccount of
an Insider  that reflects the performance of the Stock Fund (which credits could  only have been made when such individual was not
an Insider) may not be transferred, withdrawn, paid out or otherwise changed, other than (A) pursuant to the Participant’ s payment
election or the rules governing distribution in the event of the Participant’ s death (but only at such time as distribution is permitted
under the securities  rules, it being intended that a delay in the normal payment schedule occur only to the extent required by
securities rules, as permitted by Section 409A) or (B) pursuant to applicable forfeiture provisions contained in the Plan.
(c)    It is intended that the crediting of amounts to the accounts of Insiders that represents the performance of the
Stock Fund is intend ed to qualify for exemption from Section 16 under Rule 16b-3(d) under the Exchange Act. The Administrator
shall, with respect to Insiders, administer and interpret all Plan provisions in a manner consistent with such exemption.

title: Supplemental Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability)
heading: Section 8.1 Supplemental Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability) .
start_phrase: By way of clarification, the rules set forth in this Section shall be applied separately to the portion of the Participant’ s Supple mental Benefits that is subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the remainder of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits that is not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, to the extent that the Participant’ s Supplemental Electi on differs from the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
summary:
- Insider restrictions related to the Stock Fund:
  - Amounts credited to an Insider’s account cannot be transferred into a Stock Fund subaccount while the individual is an Insider.
  - Amounts in a Stock Fund subaccount that were credited when the individual was not an Insider, and any amounts in an Insider’s account, cannot be transferred, withdrawn, paid, or otherwise changed except:
    - As provided by the participant’s payment election,
    - Under death distribution rules but only when permitted by securities laws (with delays only as required and consistent with Section 409A), or
    - Under applicable forfeiture provisions.
  - The plan intends Stock Fund performance credits for Insiders to qualify for the Exchange Act Section 16 exemption under Rule 16b-3(d); the Administrator will interpret/administer the plan to preserve this exemption.

- Article 8: Payment of Benefits
  - Section 8.1 Supplemental Account Payments (other than death or disability):
    - Rules apply separately to the portion subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and to any other elected portion.
    - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (other than death or disability), within 90 days.
    - Installments: begin on July 1 of the calendar year after Separation from Service, and continue each July 1, each within 90 days.
    - Rehire after Separation does not change the established payment schedule.
    - If a participant made a one-time permissible change to the initial Supplemental Election (under Sections 5.4(a)(ii) or 5.4(d)) effective before Separation, the affected Supplemental Benefits are delayed by five years from the otherwise applicable payment/commencement date; the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election cannot be modified and is not subject to this five-year delay.
    - Installment calculation uses a declining-balance method: each payment equals the then-remaining Supplemental Benefits multiplied by 1/(number of remaining payments).
    - Payments are limited to the vested portion determined under the Qualified Retirement Plans’ vesting rules; non-vested amounts are forfeited.

  - Section 8.2 Deferral Account Payments (other than death or disability):
    - Post-2010 deferrals generally follow Section 8.1 unless a special payment election under Section 6.5 applies; Pre-2011 deferrals follow Sections 8.2(b)(i) or 8.2(c)(i).
    - Specified Date Elections for Employees in Band 50 or above:
      - If no Separation from Service, death, or Disability by the specified date, Pre-2011 deferrals are paid as elected:
        - Lump sum: on the first March 15 or September 15 after the specified date (or on that date if it is March 15 or September 15), within 90 days.
        - Installments: begin on the first March 15 or September 15 after the specified date (or on that date), and continue each March 15, each within 90 days.
text:
Section 8.1    Supplemental Account Payments (Other  than Payments Due to Death or  Disability) .
(a)    By way of clarification, the rules set forth in this Section shall be applied separately to the portion of the
Participant’ s Supple mental Benefits that is subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the remainder of the
Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits that is not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, to the extent that
the Participant’ s Supplemental Electi on differs from the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election. Subject to
Section 8.1(b), payment of Supplemen tal Benefits shall be made as follows: (i) if the governing Election calls for a lump-sum
payment, it shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’ s Separation from
Service for any reaso n (other than death  or Disability) from the Company , or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no
event later than 90 days; and (ii) if the governing Election calls for annual installment payments, they shall begin on July 1 of the
calendar year follow ing the Participant’ s Separation from Service for any reason (other than death or Disability) from the Company ,
or as soon  thereafte r as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon
thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant. A
Participant who has experienced a Sepa ration from Service and is to receive or has begun receiving payments as set forth above,
shall continue receiving any remaining payments according to the terms in effect on the date of his or her Separation from Service,
even if later re-employed by the Company .
(b)    If a Participant has made the one-time modification to his or her initial Supplemental Election pursuant to
Section 5.4(a)(ii) or Section 5.4(d) and such subsequent Supplemental Election has become effective prior to the Participant’ s
Separation from Service, then payment of such Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits (to the extent governed by the
-30-amended Election) pursuant to Section 8.1(a) shall be made, or commence in the case of annual installments, on the date that is five
years later than the date such Suppleme ntal Benefits would otherwise be made  or commence pursuant to Section 8.1(a). The rehire
of a Participant during this intervening period will not affect the payment schedule. The Automatic New Participant Supplemental
Election may not be modified, and accordingly the portion of the benefit subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental
Election will not be subject to any five-year delay .
(c)    If a Participant has elected annual  installment payments, each annual installment payment shall be determined
by multiplying the amount of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits by a fraction, the numerator of which is one, and the
denominator of which is the number of remaining payments (e.g., if the Participant elected five installments, the first annual
installment payment would be the amount of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits multiplied by 1/5, the second annual
installment payment would be the remaining amount of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits multiplied by 1/4, etc.).
(d)    The payment of Supplemental Benefits to a Participant under this Section 8.1 shall be limited to a Participant’ s
vested portion of his or her Supplemental Account at the time of distribution. Unless otherwise expressly provided in the Plan, a
Participant’ s vested portion shall be determined under the vesting provisions of the Qualified Retirement Plans. Any non-vested
portion of amounts credited to a Participant hereunder shall be forfeited.

title: Deferral Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability)
heading: Section 8.2 Deferral Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability) .
start_phrase: With respect to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, payments not made on accoun t of death or Disability will be governed by Section 8.1 except to the extent that a Participant was eligible to make a special payment election with respect to such Deferral Benefits pursuant to Section 6.5, in which case payment will be governed by Section 8.2(b) or Section 8.2(c), as applicable.
summary:
- Supplemental Benefits (Section 8.1): 
  - If a participant amends an election under 8.1(a), payments (or the start of installments) are delayed five years from the original 8.1(a) date; rehire during this period does not change the schedule.
  - The Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election cannot be modified and is not subject to the five-year delay.
  - Annual installments are paid using a declining-fraction method: each payment equals the then-remaining Supplemental Benefits multiplied by 1 divided by the number of remaining payments.
  - Payments are limited to the vested portion of the Supplemental Account; non-vested amounts are forfeited (vesting per the Qualified Retirement Plans).

- Deferral Account Payments other than for death or disability (Section 8.2):
  - General rule: Post-2010 Deferral Benefits follow Section 8.1 unless a special payment election under 6.5 applies; Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits follow 8.2(b)(i) or 8.2(c)(i).
  - Specified date elections for Employees in Band 50 or above (8.2(b)):
    - Pre-2011: 
      - Lump sum: paid on the first March 15 or September 15 following the specified date (or on that date if chosen), within 90 days.
      - Installments: begin on the first March 15 or September 15 following (or on) the specified date, then each March 15 within 90 days for the elected period.
      - If Separation from Service occurs before all installments are paid: if Retirement Eligible, continue as scheduled; if not, remaining installments convert to a lump sum under 8.2(c)(i).
    - Post-2010:
      - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date, within 90 days.
      - Installments: begin on the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date, then each January 1 or July 1 within 90 days for the elected period.
      - If Separation from Service occurs before completion, remaining installments continue as scheduled.
  - Separation from Service for Employees in Band 50 or above (8.2(c))—applies regardless of any later specified date:
    - Pre-2011:
      - Retirement Eligible: 
        - Lump sum: paid on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, within 90 days.
        - Installments: begin on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, then each March 15 within 90 days for the elected period.
        - Re-employment does not change the existing schedule.
      - Not Retirement Eligible: all Deferral Benefits are paid in a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, within 90 days.
    - Post-2010:
      - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, within 90 days.
      - Installments: begin on the first July 1 in the calendar year following separation, then each July 1 within 90 days for the elected period.
      - Re-employment does not change the existing schedule.
  - Installment calculation (8.2(d)): declining-fraction method using 1 divided by the number of remaining payments (e.g., 1/5, then 1/4 of the remaining balance, etc.).
  - Payments limited to vested Deferral Account amounts; non-vested amounts are forfeited (8.2(e)).

- Beneficiary designations (Section 8.3): 
  - Participants may separately designate beneficiaries for the Supplemental Account and the Deferral Account, and may revoke/modify at any time via the Administrator’s prescribed form.
  - Designation is automatically revoked upon the beneficiary’s death or, if the beneficiary is the spouse, upon divorce.
  - If no designation is in effect when due, the beneficiary is the surviving spouse; if none, the participant’s estate.

Section 8.2    Deferral Account Payments (Other  than Payments Due to Death or  Disability) .
(a)    Generally Applicabl e Rules for Payment to Participants . With respect to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, payments
not made on accoun t of death or Disability will be governed by Section 8.1 except to the extent that a Participant was eligible to
make a special payment election with respect to such Deferral Benefits pursuant to Section 6.5, in which case payment will be
governed by Section 8.2(b) or Section 8.2(c), as applicable. Pre-201 1 Deferral Benefits not payable on account of death or Disability
will be paid in accordance with Section 8.2(b)(i) or Section 8.2(c)(i), as applicable.
(b)    Specified Date Elections for Employees  in Band 50 or Above . If a Participant designated a specified date as the
time when  some or all of the Deferral Benefits of such Participant are to be paid, and the Participant has not had a Separation from
Service, died or incurred a Disability as of the specified date, then payment of the Deferral Account shall be made as follows:
(i)    In the case of Pre-201 1 Deferral Benefits, (A) if the Participant elected a lump-sum payment of some or
all of such Deferral Benefits, it shall be made on the first March 15 or September 15 following the specified date (or if the
Participant designated March 15 or September 15 as the specified date, payment shall be made on such specified date), or as soon
thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days; and (B) if the Participant elected annual installment
payments of some or all of such Deferral Benefits, payment shall begin on the first March 15 or September 15 following the
specified date (or if the Participant designated March 15 or September 15 as the specified date, payment shall begin on such
specified date), or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each
March 15 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible,
-31-but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant. If a Participant who is to receive or has begun
receiving payments in annual installments under this Section 8.2(b)(i) experiences a Separation from Service before having received
all of the annual installments to which the Participant is entitled, then if the Parti cipant is Retirement Eligible at the time of his or her
Separation from Service, the Participant shall receive or continue to receive the remaining annual installment payments as scheduled,
and if the Participant is not Retirement  Eligible at the time of his or her Separ ation from Service, then the remaining installments
shall be paid to the Participant in a lump sum pursuant to Section 8.2(c)(i).
(ii)    In the case of Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, (A) if the Participant elected a lump-sum payment of some or
all of such Deferral Benefits, it shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date or as
soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and (B) if the Participant elected annual installment
payments of some or all of such Deferra l Benefits, payment shall begin on the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following
the specified date, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and continue each January 1
or July 1 (as applic able) thereafter (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) for the
period selected by the Participant. If a Participant who is to receive or has begun receiving payments in annual installments under
this Section 8.2(b)(ii) experiences a Separation from Service before having received all of the annual installments to which the
Participant is entitled, then the Partici pant shall receive or continue to receive the remaining annual installment payments as
scheduled.
(c)    Separation from Service for Employees in Band 50 or Above . If a Participant has a Separation from Service for
any reason other than death or Disability , regardless of whether the Participant designated a later specified date as the time when
some or all Deferra l Benefits are to be paid, then Deferral Benefits subject to a Deferral Election that specifies time and form of
payment under Section 6.5 will be paid as follows:
(i)    In the case of Pre-201 1 Deferral Benefits:
(A)    If a Participa nt is Retirement Eligible at the time of his or her Separation from Service, then
payment of the Participant’ s Deferral Benefits shall be made as follows: (A) if the Participant elected a lump-sum payment of some
or all Defe rral Bene fits, payment of such Deferral Benefits shall be made on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six
months following the Participant’ s Separation from Service from the Company , or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but
in no event later than 90 days; and (B) if the Participant elected annual installment payments of some or all Deferral Benefits,
payment of such Deferral Benefits shall begin on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the
Participant’ s Separat ion from Service from the Company , or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than
90 days, and shall continue on each March 15 (or as soon thereafter as adminis tratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days)
thereafter for the period selected by the Participant. A Participant who has exper ienced a Separation from Service and is to receive or
has begun receiving payments as set forth above, shall continue receiving any remaining payments according to the terms in effect
on the date of his or her Separation from Service, even if later re-employed by the Company .
-32-(B)    If a Participan t is not Retirement Eligible at the time of his or her Separat ion from Service, then
regardless of the Participant’ s Deferral Elections, payment of all of the Participant’ s Deferral Benefits shall be made in a lump sum
on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’ s Separation from Service, or as soon
thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.
(ii)    In the case of Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, upon Separation from Service, payment of the Participant’ s
Deferral Benefits shall be made as follows: (A) if the Participant elected a lump-sum payment of some or all Deferral Benefits,
payment of such Deferral Benefits shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the
Participant’ s Separat ion from Service from the Company , or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than
90 days; and (B) if the Participant elected annual installment payments of some or all Deferral Benefits, payment of such Deferral
Benefits shall begin on the first July 1 in the calendar year following the Participant’ s Separation from Service from the Company , or
as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon
thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant. A
Participant who has experienced a Sepa ration from Service and is to receive or has begun receiving payments as set forth above,
shall continue receiving any remaining payments according to the terms in effect on the date of his or her Separation from Service,
even if later re-employed by the Company .
(d)    Calculation of Installments . If a Participant will receive payment of some or all Deferral Benefits in annual
installment payments, each annual installment payment shall be determined by multiplying the amount of the Deferral Benefits
being paid pursuant to such Deferral Election by a fraction, the numerator of which is one, and the denominator of which is the
number of remaining payments (e.g., if the Participant is to receive payment of the entire amount in his or her Deferral Account in
five installments, the first annual install ment payment would be the amount of the Participant’ s Deferral Account multiplied by 1/5,
the second annual installment payment would be the remaining amount of such Deferral Account multiplied by 1/4, etc.).
(e)    Payment Limited to Vested Amount . The payment of a Participant’ s Deferral Account for a Plan Year under this
Section 8.2 shall be limited to a Participant’ s vested portion of his or her Deferral Account at the time of distribution. Any non-
vested portion of amounts credited to a Participant hereunder shall be forfeited.

title: Designation of Beneficiaries
heading: Section 8.3 Designation of Beneficia ries.
start_phrase: A Partici pant may separately designate a Beneficiary or Beneficiaries entitled to receive payment of his or her Supplemental Account and his or her Deferral Account by filing written notice of such designation with the Administrat or in such form as the Administrator may prescribe.
summary:
- Payment timing after Separation from Service:
  - If not Retirement Eligible: all Deferral Benefits are paid in a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, or as soon as administratively feasible within 90 days.
  - For Post-2010 Deferral Benefits:
    - If a lump sum was elected: payment on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If annual installments were elected: first payment on the first July 1 of the calendar year following separation, then each July 1 thereafter for the elected period, each within 90 days as administratively feasible.
  - Re-employment after separation does not change an established payment schedule.

- Installment calculation:
  - Each annual installment equals the current account balance for the elected portion multiplied by 1 divided by the remaining number of payments (e.g., 1/5, then 1/4, etc.).

- Vesting:
  - Distributions are limited to the vested portion of the Deferral Account at the time of payment; any non-vested amounts are forfeited.

- Beneficiary designations:
  - Participants may separately designate beneficiaries for the Supplemental Account and the Deferral Account, and may modify or revoke at any time using prescribed forms.
  - Automatic revocation occurs upon the beneficiary’s death or, if the beneficiary is the spouse, upon dissolution of marriage.
  - Default beneficiary if no designation: surviving spouse, or if none, the participant’s estate.
  - For deaths on or after January 1, 2013: spousal beneficiary designations are automatically void upon divorce, subject to any applicable domestic relations order; participants may re-designate a former spouse after divorce. Similar rules apply where a beneficiary is permitted to designate a beneficiary and later divorces that person.
  - The plan is not liable for payments made to a named beneficiary before the plan is notified of a divorce.

- Death benefits:
  - Supplemental Account:
    - If death occurs while actively employed: lump-sum payment on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments began (or during a delay due to a modified election): remaining installments are accelerated and paid as a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If death occurs after separation but before the scheduled payment date (six months after separation): payment is made to the beneficiary on the originally scheduled date. Any five-year delay due to a modified election is disregarded upon death; death benefit rules apply immediately.
  - Deferral Account (Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits):
    - If death occurs while actively employed: lump-sum payment on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments began: remaining installments are accelerated and paid as a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.

Section 8.3    Designation of Beneficia ries. A Partici pant may separately designate  a Beneficiary or Beneficiaries entitled to
receive payment of his or her Supplemental Account and his or her Deferral Account by filing written notice of such designation
with the Administrat or in such form as the Administrator may prescribe. A Participant may revoke or modify such designation at any
time by a further written designation in such form as the Administrator may prescribe. A Participant’ s Beneficiary designation shall
be deemed automatically revoked in the event of the death of the Beneficiary or, if the Beneficiary is the Participant’ s spouse, in the
event of dissolution of marriage. If no designation is in effect at the time Benefits payable under the relevant Account become due,
the Beneficiary of such Account shall be deemed to be the Participant’ s surviving spouse, if any , and if not, the Participant’ s estate.
-33-Effective for Partici pants who die on or after January 1, 2013, if a Participant has designated his or her spouse as his or her
beneficiary for either or both Accounts,  that designation shall automatically become null and void in the event of the Participant’ s
divorce, without prejudice, however , to any rights the former spouse may be granted pursuant to a domestic relations order
applicable to the Plan. In the event that a beneficiary designation is voided hereunder , the benefit shall be paid as if the former
spouse had pre-deceased the Participant. A Participant who wishes the former spouse to be his or her beneficiary may file a new
beneficiary designation form naming the former spouse after the date of divorce. These rules will also apply in the event a
beneficiary is permitted to designate a beneficiary and becomes divorced from the person named as beneficiary . Notwithstanding the
foregoing, neither the Plan nor any other person will be liable for payment made to a named beneficiary prior to the date that the
Plan is notified that such person is a divorced spouse.

title: Death
heading: Section 8.4 Death .
start_phrase: Upon a Participant’ s death, payment of the Participant’ s Supplemental Account shall be made to the Participant’ s Beneficiary or Beneficiaries designated to receive the Participant’ s Supplemental Account.
summary:
- Automatic revocation of spousal beneficiary upon divorce (effective for deaths on/after Jan 1, 2013): any spouse designation for either/both Accounts becomes void at divorce, subject to rights under a domestic relations order; benefits then paid as if former spouse predeceased the Participant. A former spouse can be re‑named via a new post‑divorce designation. Same rules apply when a beneficiary who is allowed to designate a beneficiary divorces. The Plan is not liable for payments made to a named beneficiary before it is notified of the divorce.
- Death benefits — Supplemental Account (Section 8.4(a)):
  - Paid to designated beneficiary(ies).
  - If death occurs while actively employed: paid as a single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
  - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments begin (or while awaiting installment start due to a post‑separation modification): remaining installments are converted to a single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (same 90‑day outer limit).
  - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled Jan 1/Jul 1 payment date that is six months post‑separation, payment is made on the originally scheduled date.
  - If a five‑year payment delay applied due to a modification of a Supplemental Election, death benefits are paid under these death rules without waiting for the five‑year period.
- Death benefits — Deferral Account (Section 8.4(b)):
  - Paid to designated beneficiary(ies).
  - Pre‑2011 Deferral Benefits:
    - If death while actively employed: single lump sum on the first Mar 15 or Sep 15 at least six months after death (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments begin: remaining installments paid as a single lump sum on the first Mar 15 or Sep 15 at least six months after death (same 90‑day outer limit).
    - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled Mar 15/Sep 15 date that is six months post‑separation, payment is made on the originally scheduled date.
  - Post‑2010 Deferral Benefits:
    - If death while actively employed: single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments begin (or while awaiting start due to a modification): remaining installments paid as a single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (same 90‑day limit).
    - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled Jan 1/Jul 1 date that is six months post‑separation, payment is made on the originally scheduled date.
    - If a five‑year delay applied due to a modification of a Supplemental Election that also applies to Deferral Benefits, death benefits are paid under these death rules without waiting five years.
- Disability — Supplemental Account (Section 8.5(a)):
  - Rules applied separately to amounts under the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and any differing elected amounts.
  - If lump sum was elected: paid on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after the Disability date (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
  - If installments were elected: payments begin on Jul 1 of the calendar year following Disability (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days) and continue each Jul 1 for the elected period.
- Disability — Deferral Accounts (Section 8.5(b)): section begins but details are not included in this excerpt.

title: Disability
heading: Section 8.5 Disability .
start_phrase: By way of clarification, the rules set forth in this Section shall be applied separately to the portion of the Participant’ s Supplem ental Benefits that is subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the remainder of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits that is not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, to the extent that the Participant’ s Supplemental Election differs from the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
summary:
- Death benefits and timing rules:
  - For Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, if a participant dies while employed, the account is paid in a single lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death (or as soon as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
  - If a participant elected installments and dies before or after installments begin, remaining amounts are paid to the beneficiary as a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death (within the 90-day administrative window).
  - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled six-month payment date, the lump sum is paid to the beneficiary on the originally scheduled date (or within 90 days).
  - Any prior five-year payment delay due to a modified Supplemental Election is overridden upon death; death benefit provisions control.

- Disability benefits (Section 8.5):
  - Rules apply separately to portions of Supplemental Benefits subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and any differing participant elections.
  - Supplemental Account:
    - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after disability (within 90 days).
    - Installments: begin July 1 of the calendar year following disability and continue each July 1 (each within 90 days).
  - Deferral Accounts:
    - Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits:
      - Lump sum: first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability (within 90 days).
      - Installments: begin the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability and continue each March 15 (each within 90 days).
    - Post-2010 Deferral Benefits:
      - Lump sum: first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after disability (within 90 days).
      - Installments: begin July 1 of the calendar year following disability and continue each July 1 (each within 90 days).

- Unforeseeable Emergency withdrawals (Section 8.6):
  - Participant may request a partial or full payout limited to the lesser of the vested Account balance or the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus anticipated taxes/penalties.
  - No payout if the need can be met by insurance/reimbursement, asset liquidation (without severe hardship), or stopping deferrals.
  - Upon approval, payment is a lump sum on the approval date or as soon as feasible, but no later than 90 days.
  - Administrator decides how the payment is allocated across accounts/subaccounts, consistent with Section 409A.

- Company offset (Section 8.7):
  - To the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, amounts otherwise payable may be forfeited or payments suspended to satisfy Company claims, including enforcement of detrimental conduct provisions, recovery of debts, or benefit overpayments.

title: Unforeseeable Emergency
heading: Section 8.6 Unfor eseeable Emergency .
start_phrase: If a Participant experiences an Unforeseeable Emer gency , the Participant may petition the Administrator to receive a partial or full payout from the Plan.
summary:
- Disability distribution timing:
  - Pre-2011 deferrals: 
    - Lump sum paid on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability (or as soon as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - Installments begin on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability (or as soon feasible, but no later than 90 days) and continue each March 15 for the elected period (same 90-day administrative window).
  - Post-2010 deferrals:
    - Lump sum paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after disability (or as soon feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - Installments begin on July 1 of the calendar year following disability (or as soon feasible, but no later than 90 days) and continue each July 1 for the elected period (same 90-day window).

- Unforeseeable Emergency withdrawals (Section 8.6):
  - Participant may petition for a payout limited to the lesser of the vested account balance or the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus anticipated taxes/penalties.
  - Not available if the emergency can be alleviated by insurance/other compensation, liquidation of assets that wouldn’t itself cause severe hardship, or by ceasing deferrals.
  - If approved, paid in a lump sum on approval or as soon as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days.
  - Administrator decides, consistent with Section 409A, how payments are applied across the participant’s account and subaccounts.

- Company offset/clawback (Section 8.7):
  - To the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, amounts otherwise payable may be forfeited or suspended to satisfy Company claims.
  - Includes enforcement of detrimental conduct provisions under the long-term incentive plan, recovery of debts to the Company, or recovery of benefit overpayments.
  - Applies notwithstanding any contrary terms in the Plan, RP, or RSP.
text:
Section 8.6    Unfor eseeable Emergency . If a Participant experiences an Unforeseeable Emer gency , the Participant may
petition the Administrator to receive a partial or full payout from the Plan. The payout, if any, from the Plan shall not exceed the
lesser of (a) the Participant’ s vested Account balance, or (b) the amount necessary to satisfy the Unforeseeable Emer gency , plus
amounts necessary to pay federal, state, or local income taxes or penalties reasonably anticipated as a result of the distribution. A
Participant shall not be eligible to receive a payout from the Plan to the extent that the Unforeseeable Emer gency is or may be
relieved (i) through reimbursement or compensation by insurance or otherwise, (ii) by liquidation of the Participant’ s assets, to the
extent the liquidatio n of such assets would not itself cause severe financial hardship or (iii) by cessation of a Deferral Election under
this Plan. If the Administrator , in its sole discretion, approves a Participant’ s petition for payout from the Plan, such payout shall be
made in a lump sum on the date on which such approval occurs, or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter , but in no event
later than 90 days. At the time of its determination, and to the extent permissible by Section 409A, the Administrator shall determine
how any payment under this Section 8.6 will be applied against the Participant’ s Account and the subaccounts thereunder .

title: Company Offset
heading: Section 8.7 Company Offset .
start_phrase: Notwiths tanding anything in the Plan, the RP or the RSP to the contrary , to the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, any amount otherwise due or payable under the Plan may be forfeited, or its payment suspended, at the discretion of the Administrator , to apply toward or recover any claim the Company may have against the Participant, including but not limited to, for the enforcement of Amex’ s Detrimental Conduct provisions under its long-term incentive award plan, to recover a debt to the Company or to recover a benefit overpayment under a Company benefit plan or program.
summary:
- Disability distributions: Specifies payment timing for Deferral Benefits upon a Participant’s Disability, distinguishing between Pre-2011 and Post-2010 deferrals and between lump-sum and installment elections. Pre-2011 payouts occur on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after Disability (with a “no later than 90 days” administrative window). Post-2010 lump sums occur on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Disability; Post-2010 installments begin July 1 of the calendar year following Disability and continue annually, each subject to the same administrative window.
- Unforeseeable Emergency withdrawals: Participants may petition for a lump-sum distribution limited to the lesser of the vested Account balance or the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus expected taxes/penalties. No payout if the need can be met by insurance, non-hardship asset liquidation, or stopping deferrals. Administrator has sole discretion; payment is made promptly but no later than 90 days, with allocation across subaccounts determined consistent with Section 409A.
- Company offset/clawback: To the extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, the Administrator may forfeit or suspend plan payments to satisfy Company claims (e.g., enforcement of Amex detrimental conduct provisions, debts, or benefit overpayments), with offsets only when amounts would otherwise be distributable and in accordance with the Company’s Section 409A policy.
- Tax withholding: The Company may withhold required income and employment taxes from any payment or require the Participant to pay such taxes in advance, subject to Section 409A.
- De minimis cash-out: The Administrator may mandate a lump-sum payout of small balances equal to the Account’s lump-sum value, not exceeding the Code Section 402(g)(1)(B) limit, provided it liquidates the Participant’s entire interest in this and all similar account balance arrangements under Treas. Reg. 1.409A-1(c)(2).
- Change in Control (partial definition): Defines a Change in Control, in part, as a Person acquiring 25% or more of Amex’s outstanding common shares or voting securities, with exceptions for acquisitions by Amex, its subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, underwriters, certain 13G filers (until switching to 13D), and some reorganization/merger scenarios (definition continues beyond the excerpt).

title: Withholding
heading: Section 8.8 Withholding .
